cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Lifecycle
cards.back: Stars form in nebulae: gravity pulls gas and dust together, forming a protostar that heats up until fusion begins

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Lifecycle
cards.back: Main sequence: the longest stable phase where hydrogen fuses to helium in the core; the Sun is currently here

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Lifecycle
cards.back: Low-mass stars (<8 solar masses) expand to red giants, shed outer layers as planetary nebulae, leaving white dwarfs

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Lifecycle
cards.back: High-mass stars (>8 solar masses) expand to red supergiants, then explode as supernovae, leaving neutron stars or black holes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Lifecycle
cards.back: The Chandrasekhar limit (~1.4 solar masses) is the maximum mass of a white dwarf

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Lifecycle
cards.back: Black holes form when the core remnant exceeds ~3 solar masses (the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff limit)
